title: Gender-Specific Differences in Immune Responses to Influenza Vaccination in People Living with HIV and Control Subjects Without Known HIV Infection
summary: This study systematically investigates the immune response in individuals who have received an influenza vaccine in line with clinical indications based on guidelines. Participants living with HIV are included to provide a more detailed understanding of their immune responses. Additionally, a control group of participants without known HIV infection who meet the STIKO criteria for influenza vaccination will be included. Once informed consent has been obtained from the participants, blood samples will be collected and nasal swabs taken. These biological samples will be analysed to investigate immune responses to the influenza vaccine.
conditions: Sex-specific immune response after influenza vaccination

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
(1)    Written informed consent for a prospective, observational study     
(2)   Healthy control subjects
(3)    People living with HIV with an indication for seasonal influenza vaccination
(4)    Influenza vaccination when indicated according to STIKO recommendations
(5)    No acute febrile illness or acute respiratory infection at the time of vaccination (in accordance with STIKO recommendations)
Exclusion criteria:
(1)    Inability to adequately understand the content and procedures of the study.
(2)    Life circumstances that, in the opinion of the investigator, could interfere with the conduct of the study, e.g., a lack of willingness to cooperate or an anticipated inability to attend further study visits due to physical weakness
(3)   Infection or vaccination (other than COVID-19) within the last 30 days
